newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil stevedores to hold national strike April 4.
newsitem.headline: Brazil stevedores to hold national strike April 4.

text.p: Brazilian stevedores will definitely hold a national 24-hour strike from 0700 local/1000 GMT on April 4, said the president of the Stevedores Federation.
"There will be a national strike on April 4," Abelardo Fernandes told Reuters by telephone.
Fernandes is in Santos where he is helping the local union in negotiations after Santos stevedores began a two-day strike at 0700 local/1000 GMT this morning.

The stevedores are striking because of a court ruling which has allowed company workers from steel mill Companhia Siderurgica Paulista (Cosipa) to conduct loading and unloading at Cosipa's private terminal at the port.
Stevedores argue under the government's port privatization program, only registered, qualified workers are allowed to carry out these operations.
Negotiations with Cosipa today have not made any advances, Fernandes said.
"Cosipa is coming to us with nothing," Fernandes said.
Federation officials will evaluate the impact of the April 4 strike to see if there is need for further action, he added.
"It's possible that there may be more stoppages than this," Fernandes said.
Other unions are discussing today whether to join the April 4 strike, said the administrative and financial secretary of the National Portworkers Federation.
"There are talks going on throughout the day. It could well be a complete strike," said Jose Horatio Freitas.
However, even if the stoppage is limited to stevedores, most ports are expected to be effectively brought to a halt, union officials said.
In Santos, only three of the 17 vessels docked at the port authority terminal were operating as of this morning due to the stevedores strike.
The three vessels were loading tallow, liquid gas and oil.
Previous strikes at Santos have hit shipments of sugar, soybeans and coffee.
